jamie: hey team — saw a spike in errors for /api/generate around 11:22. I have a request_id: request_7f9a2b and a trace id: 0x9f3c4a. can someone help me find the raw logs?

ravi: start in Console -> Observability -> Request Explorer. paste the request_id into the search box; it usually links directly to spans + logs. if you only have trace id, use Trace Search and then click the linked request.

sofia: quick CLI fallback if Console is slow:
```
# search logs by request id (our internal CLI)
redwood logs find --request-id request_7f9a2b --since 30m

# if you only have trace id
redwood traces show 0x9f3c4a --expand-requests
```

lee: alternative raw grep (if you have access to logstore buckets):
```bash
# fetch last hour of app logs and grep for request id
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/prod/app/2026-03-17/ - | zcat | grep request_7f9a2b | head -n 50
```

jamie: thanks — ran the CLI and got a couple lines but not the KV-cache logs I expected. the trace shows a downstream model timeout at span 43. any tips to find the model-serving logs?

ravi: model-serving logs are under a different prefix. try:
```
redwood logs find --service model-serving --trace-id 0x9f3c4a --since 1h
```
if that returns nothing, add --raw to include infra logs.

sofia: also check the Request Explorer's "Related Logs" panel — it surfaces cache hits/misses and model requests. the trace span should have an attribute like service=redwood-model or resource=model-serving-1.

lee: if you want a single combined view we have an internal helper that collates traces+logs: 
```
redwood debug correlate --trace 0x9f3c4a --output short
# outputs a timeline with span timestamps + log snippets
```

jamie: ran correlate and found the model-serving host id (ms-42). pulling its logs now.

ops-bot: <https://console.redwood.ai/observability/requests/request_7f9a2b|Open Request in Console> :link:

sofia: if you end up needing a quick alert tuned, drop the final signal (error type + host). we can add a temporary suppression or raise a more specific alert for model timeouts.

jamie: will do, thanks everyone. pinging infra if this keeps happening. :thumbsup:

ravi: fyi: common gotcha — request ids from older clients include a prefix (req:) so try both forms if nothing shows up.

lee: adding checklist for runbook: 1) Console Request Explorer -> 2) redwood logs find (request_id) -> 3) redwood traces show (trace) -> 4) redwood debug correlate -> 5) escalate to model infra

jamie: saved the checklist in the incident doc. closing unless it reappears.
